5 ترغّم (assumed tropical:) He became angered, or angry, (S, K, TA,) with speech, and otherwise: (TA:) and sometimes it occurs with ز [i. e. تزغّم]. (S, TA.) Hence the saying of El-Hotei-ah, [app. describing a she-camel,] “تَرَى بَيْنَ لَحْيَيْهَا إِذَا مَا تَرَغَّمَتْ
لُغَامًا كَبَيْتِ العَنْكَبُوتِ الُمَدَّدِ
” [Thou seest between her two jaws, when she is angered, foam like the web of the spider stretched out]. (TA.) ＝
-A2- See also 1.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
